transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-06-01
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah, Marcus Liu (Redwood) / Lara Mendes, Benji Ortega, Sanjay Rao, Maya Finch (ContractOxygen)

Summary sections may be auto-generated. Transcript below is imperfect — occasional mislabels and phonetic errors included.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? I'm Alex, I'll run the commercial side, Priya here will run through the technical bits.
[00:12] Lara Mendes: Hi, Lara here — procurement. We're running this as the vendor onboarding kickoff, trying to close the MSA and DPA and get clarity on SLA targets and pricing path.
[00:22] Benji Ortega: Benji, InfoSec. I'll be focused on controls, encryption, audit.
[00:27] Priya Shah: Priya Shah, systems engineer at Redwood, I'll do the infra/architecture and benchmarks portion.
[00:32] Sanjay Rao: Sanjay, platform engineering — I'll be the technical owner for the pilot.
[00:36] Maya Finch: Maya, legal. I'll be reviewing contractual language, DPA and any data residency clauses.

[00:45] Alex Kim: Great. Agenda for today: status of MSA redlines, DPA clarifications, SLA targets, quick walk through deployment options (hosted / dedicated / private), pricing/egress questions, and next steps.

[01:05] Lara: For context we have two parallel constraints — one is regulatory: EU data residency for a subset of PII, and second is our procurement bar for uptime — we need 99.95 for core endpoints. We also have FinOps constraints around egress.

[01:30] Priya: Understood. Quick note on deployment: Hosted is fastest, gives you immediate production — but egress lines are charged at per-GB; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and better predictability; Private (VPC/On-prem) lets you keep keys on-prem or in your KMS and satisfies strict residency, but has a longer lead time.

[01:58] Benji: On KMS — are you able to integrate with customer-managed KMS? We need to ensure HSM-level key wrapping. How does that look?

[02:12] Marcus Liu: Yes, we support external KMS integrations and HSM-backed key management. For Private deployments you can bring your KMS and we can configure the crypto boundary so Redwood does not hold plaintext keys. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood KMS or customer KMS via an HSM connector. There's some work on the network and key rotation to finalize.

[02:45] Maya: On the DPA, we need explicit language about subprocessors and a right to audit clause. Our legal team is asking for 30 days' notice for subprocessor changes and a commensurate audit window.

[03:05] Alex: Noted — we usually include a subprocessor list and a 30- to 60-day notification window. Audit access is possible but we typically provide SOC2 reports and an audit assistance path; direct full audits are rarer but we can discuss a scoped audit.

[03:29] Lara: The SLA — 99.95 is our ask but we also want a clear escalation path and credits for downtime. Can you map the proposed SLA tiers to your pricing?

[03:45] Alex: For Dedicated we can commit to 99.95 with an SLA credit schedule in the MSA. Hosted has variable availability tiers; we can work a commitment for higher tiers in a reserved capacity contract. Pricing delta depends on commit level and whether you need cross-region failover; I'll follow up with a pricing model.

[04:10] Sanjay: A more technical question — how do you manage KV cache persistence for long session chats? There's been some confusion in the doc where 'KV cache' was typed as 'K V cash' so i wanted to confirm the behavior.

[04:26] Priya: Yeah, apologies for the OCR typos. Our runtime handles KV cache in-memory per session and we can persist hot prefixes to a cache layer for warm starts. For Private deployments we can pin cache nodes to avoid eviction during rolling upgrades.

[04:47] Benji: Audit logs — retention windows and tamper-proofing? We need 7 years for some flows.

[04:55] Marcus: We support configurable log retention; for Hosted we store audit logs in an immutable bucket with append-only semantics; for Private you can ship logs to your SIEM or GCP/OCI/AWS bucket with lifecycle policies. For 7 years, that's feasible but may incur storage costs which we'll itemize.

[05:18] Maya: Also need SSO/SAML/SCIM integration and RBAC in the product. Can you confirm supported IdPs?

[05:28] Priya: Standard SAML and OIDC flows — AD/Okta/Azure Okta and other SAML providers are supported. SCIM provisioning and role-based access can be scoped per team.

[05:45] Lara: Pricing — our procurement wants to see egress and per-token cost broken out. We have big concerns about token billing unpredictability during spikes.

[06:00] Alex: We can provide a cost model — tokens, embeddings, and per-GB egress. For Dedicated we can offer committed throughput with overage rates; for Hosted we recommend a burst policy and throttles. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization to reduce unit cost.

[06:22] Sanjay: For the pilot — we're planning a small POC with 100k monthly requests and some heavy long-context sessions. We want to test latency in EU region and a failover to US.

[06:35] Priya: For that load, Dedicated small pool should be fine. We'll run a benchmark that mirrors your session lengths and report median P95 latency and token cost. Priya to provide spreadsheet.

[06:50] Benji: Data residency for PII — can you guarantee that certain model inferences never leave EU region? We're evaluating both Hosted with region pinning and Private.

[07:05] Marcus: Region pinning is supported at route level in hosted mode with policy routing. Private deployment gives absolute locality. We'll note any cross-region backups or telemetry flows which may need extra clauses.

[07:28] Maya: On indemnity and liability caps — our legal wants language around data breach remediation and incident response SLA windows (e.g., notify within 72 hours).

[07:42] Alex: We typically have incident notification clauses and a 72-hour notification for breaches; the liability cap will need to be negotiated — we'll put our standard commercial terms in the redline and flag the indemnity sections for discussion.

[08:02] Lara: Is Redwood able to accept a customer-specific DPA amendment or do you require using your standard DPA?

[08:12] Alex: We have a standard DPA but can accept a customer DPA as an addendum if it doesn't introduce incompatibilities with subprocessors or technical constraints. We'll need the legal team to triage any non-standard asks.

[08:28] Sanjay: Network egress — we want to estimate monthly egress from EU for model outputs; do you have average output size per generation?"

[08:42] Priya: Depends on prompt length and token counts. For text generation an average output might be 500 tokens -> roughly 400KB per response, but that's variable. We'll provide a conservative per-response estimate and model three scenarios.

[09:02] Benji: Any concerns around model weights or IP? We might want to host an open model in private so we control weights.

[09:13] Marcus: Private deployment supports customer-hosted model artifacts; our runtime will run against your weights in your environment. For hosting open models we can assist with model onboarding and quantization recommendations.

[09:32] Maya: Subprocessors list — can you share current list? Also any plans to add new cloud regions or partners?

[09:42] Alex: We'll attach the current subprocessor list in the redline packet. Future additions will be notified; typical partners include CDN providers and cloud KMS connectors.

[09:55] Lara: For timeline — procurement would like to close commercial terms within two weeks and have a pilot starting mid-June. Can Redwood meet that?

[10:05] Alex: If we get the DPA/MSA redline back quickly and the technical preflight is green, mid-June pilot is feasible. Priya: any blocking technical items?

[10:14] Priya: We need their network topology and any restrictive egress firewall rules. Sanjay to share. Also we should run an initial hosted benchmark while private setup is provisioned.

[10:26] Sanjay: I'll send topology and a list of IP allowlists. Also need a list of required audit controls.

[10:34] Benji: Regarding SOC2 and framework — do you have FedRAMP or ISO compliance?

[10:39] Marcus: We have SOC2 Type II and are pursuing ISO 27001; FedRAMP is not in place today. We'll provide our attestations and third-party audit reports.

[10:54] Maya: On the MSA language for SLA credits and termination — we may ask for shorter cure periods for critical outages.

[11:02] Alex: We'll propose standard cure timelines but we can discuss shorter windows for critical SLOs.

[11:12] Lara: Can you also outline rollback / fallback policies if a region suffers outage? We need a plan for graceful degradation.

[11:22] Priya: We have automatic fallback to compatible model variants and region routing policies; during outages we can route to lower-latency or lower-cost variants — that's part of the routing/fallback playbook. We'll document the exact policy for the pilot.

[11:42] Benji: One last security ask: key rotation cadence and access audits for Redwood staff.

[11:50] Marcus: Rotation can be configured monthly or quarterly; for Hosted we rotate them and publish rotation logs. Access by Redwood staff is controlled by RBAC and just-in-time elevation and recorded in audit logs.

[12:05] Alex: Okay let's recap next steps. I'll send the MSA + initial DPA redline and the subprocessors list. Priya will send benchmark spreadsheet and cost scenarios. Sanjay will share topology. Maya to send list of legal must-haves. We'll target a follow-up on 2027-06-07 to lock SLAs and schedule the technical deep dive.

[12:30] Maya: Sounds good. Any competitor questions — are you leveraging any third-party inference partners?

[12:38] Alex: We partner with some infra firms for dedicated pools but the inference engine is Redwood-owned; we also benchmark against Anthropic and OpenAI but we don't proxy calls.

[12:50] Lara: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the DPA feedback over in 48 hours.

[13:00] Alex Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up with materials today/tomorrow.

End transcript. Some timestamps are approximate — full meeting recorded for compliance.
